sanskrit: prasīda mama bhaktasya dīnasya kṛpaṇasya ca anaiśvaryeṇa yuktasya gatir bhava sanātana
english: Be gracious to me, your devotee, wretched and forlorn, beset by helplessness; be my refuge, O eternal one.

sanskrit: yaṃ cāparādhaṃ kṛtavān ajñānāt parameśvara madbhakta iti deveśa tat sarvaṃ kṣantum arhasi
english: Whatever offense I have committed in ignorance, O supreme lord, deign to forgive it all, O lord of gods, for I am your devotee.

sanskrit: mohitaś cāsmi deveśa tubhyaṃ rūpaviparyayāt tena nārghyaṃ mayā dattaṃ pādyaṃ cāpi sureśvara
english: I was deluded, O lord of gods, by the disguise of your form, and so I offered you neither the welcome-water nor the water for your feet, O lord of the celestials.

sanskrit: evaṃ stutvāham īśānaṃ pādyam arghyaṃ ca bhaktitaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā sarvaṃ tasmai nyavedayam
english: Having thus praised Īśāna, with hands folded in reverence I offered him in devotion the water for his feet, the water of welcome, and all the rites.

sanskrit: tataḥ śītāmbusaṃyuktā divyagandhasamanvitā puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ śubhā tāta papāta mama mūrdhani
english: Then, O dear one, a gracious shower of flowers, cool with water and fragrant with celestial scents, fell upon my head.

sanskrit: dundubhiś ca tato divyas tāḍito devakiṃkaraiḥ vavau ca mārutaḥ puṇyaḥ śucigandhaḥ sukhāvahaḥ
english: Then a celestial kettledrum was sounded by the servants of the gods, and a holy breeze blew, pure-scented and bringing delight.

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ sapatnīko vṛṣadhvajaḥ abravīt tridaśāṃs tatra harṣayann iva māṃ tadā
english: Then Mahādeva, the bull-bannered one, well pleased and accompanied by his consort, spoke to the gods, gladdening me as it were.

sanskrit: paśyadhvaṃ tridaśāḥ sarve upamanyor mahātmanaḥ mayi bhaktiṃ parāṃ divyām ekabhāvād avasthitām
english: Behold, all you gods, the supreme and celestial devotion of the great-souled Upamanyu toward me, established in singleness of heart.

sanskrit: evam uktās tataḥ kṛṣṇa surās te śūlapāṇinā ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve namaskṛtvā vṛṣadhvajam
english: Thus addressed by the trident-bearer, O Kṛṣṇa, all those gods, with folded hands and bowing to the bull-bannered one, replied:

sanskrit: bhagavan devadeveśa lokanātha jagatpate labhatāṃ sarvakāmebhyaḥ phalaṃ tvatto dvijottamaḥ
english: O lord, O god of gods and ruler of gods, O protector of worlds, master of the universe, let this best of the twice-born obtain from you the fruit of all his desires.

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ śarvaḥ surair brahmādibhis tathā āha māṃ bhagavān īśaḥ prahasann iva śaṃkaraḥ
english: Thus addressed by the gods led by Brahmā, Śarva—the lord, Śaṃkara—spoke to me as though smiling:

sanskrit: vatsopamanyo prīto 'smi paśya māṃ munipuṃgava dṛḍhabhakto 'si viprarṣe mayā jijñāsito hy asi
english: My child Upamanyu, I am pleased; behold me, O bull among sages. You are firm in devotion, O brahmin seer, and I have tested you.

sanskrit: anayā caiva bhaktyā te atyarthaṃ prītimān aham tasmāt sarvān dadāmy adya kāmāṃs tava yathepśitān
english: By this devotion of yours I am exceedingly delighted; therefore I grant you this day all the desires you wish for.

sanskrit: evam uktasya caivātha mahādevena me vibho harṣād aśrūṇy avartanta lomaharṣaś ca jāyate
english: When Mahādeva had thus spoken to me, O mighty one, tears flowed from joy, and my hair stood on end.

sanskrit: abruvaṃ ca tadā devaṃ harṣagadgadayā girā jānubhyām avaniṃ gatvā praṇamya ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: And then, touching the earth with my knees and bowing again and again, I addressed the god in a voice faltering with joy:

sanskrit: adya jāto hy ahaṃ deva adya me saphalaṃ tapaḥ yan me sākṣān mahādevaḥ prasannas tiṣṭhate 'grataḥ
english: Today indeed am I born, O god; today my austerity has borne fruit, in that Mahādeva himself stands graciously before me.

sanskrit: yaṃ na paśyanti cārādhya devā hy amitavikramam tam ahaṃ dṛṣṭavān devaṃ ko 'nyo dhanyataro mayā
english: That god of boundless might, whom even the gods cannot behold for all their worship, I have now beheld; who is more blessed than I?

sanskrit: evaṃ dhyāyanti vidvāṃsaḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ sanātanam ṣaḍviṃśakam iti khyātaṃ yat parātparam akṣaram
english: Thus do the wise meditate upon him as the supreme eternal principle, known as the twenty-sixth, the imperishable, higher than the highest.

sanskrit: sa eṣa bhagavān devaḥ sarvatattvādir avyayaḥ sarvatattvavidhānajñaḥ pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ
english: This same lord, the imperishable god, is the source of all principles, knower of the ordering of all principles, the master of Primal Nature and Spirit.

sanskrit: yo 'sṛjad dakṣiṇād aṅgād brahmāṇaṃ lokasaṃbhavam vāmapārśvāt tathā viṣṇuṃ lokarakṣārtham īśvaraḥ yugānte caiva saṃprāpte rudram aṅgāt sṛjat prabhuḥ
english: It was the lord who created from his right side Brahmā, the origin of the worlds, and from his left side Viṣṇu for the protection of the worlds; and when the age's end arrives, the master brings forth Rudra from his body.

sanskrit: sa rudraḥ saṃharan kṛtsnaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam kālo bhūtvā mahātejāḥ saṃvartaka ivānalaḥ
english: That Rudra, of great splendor, withdrawing the whole world of things moving and unmoving, becomes Time itself, like the all-consuming fire of dissolution.

sanskrit: eṣa devo mahādevo jagat sṛṣṭvā carācaram kalpānte caiva sarveṣāṃ smṛtim ākṣipya tiṣṭhati
english: This god, Mahādeva, having created the world of things moving and unmoving, at the end of the aeon withdraws the consciousness of all and abides alone.

sanskrit: sarvagaḥ sarvabhūtātmā sarvabhūtabhavodbhavaḥ āste sarvagato nityam adṛśyaḥ sarvadaivataiḥ
english: All-pervading, the self of all beings, the source from which all beings arise, he abides forever present everywhere, unseen even by all the gods.

sanskrit: yadi deyo varo mahyaṃ yadi tuṣṭaś ca me prabhuḥ bhaktir bhavatu me nityaṃ śāśvatī tvayi śaṃkara
english: If a boon is to be granted to me, and if my lord is pleased with me, then let my devotion to you, O Śaṃkara, be everlasting and eternal.

sanskrit: atītānāgataṃ caiva vartamānaṃ ca yad vibho jānīyām iti me buddhis tvatprasādāt surottama
english: And that I may know what is past, what is to come, and what is present, O mighty one—such is my wish—by your grace, O best of the gods.

sanskrit: kṣīrodanaṃ ca bhuñjīyām akṣayaṃ saha bāndhavaiḥ āśrame ca sadā mahyaṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ param astu te
english: And that I may eat of inexhaustible milk-rice together with my kinsmen, and that your supreme presence may ever abide for me in my hermitage.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa māṃ prāha bhagavāṃl lokapūjitaḥ maheśvaro mahātejāś carācaraguruḥ prabhuḥ
english: Thus addressed, the lord—Maheśvara, worshiped by all the worlds, of great splendor, the master and teacher of all things moving and unmoving—said to me:

sanskrit: ajaraś cāmaraś caiva bhava duḥkhavivarjitaḥ śīlavān guṇasaṃpannaḥ sarvajñaḥ priyadarśanaḥ
english: Be free from age and free from death, released from sorrow, virtuous, endowed with every excellence, all-knowing, and fair to look upon.

sanskrit: akṣayaṃ yauvanaṃ te 'stu tejaś caivānalopamam kṣīrodaḥ sāgaraś caiva yatra yatrecchase mune
english: Let your youth be unfading and your splendor like fire, and let the ocean of milk be present wherever you wish, O sage.

sanskrit: tatra te bhavitā kāmaṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ payaso nidheḥ kṣīrodanaṃ ca bhuṅkṣva tvam amṛtena samanvitam
english: There the presence of the ocean of milk shall be yours at will, and you shall eat milk-rice mingled with the nectar of immortality.

sanskrit: bandhubhiḥ sahitaḥ kalpaṃ tato mām upayāsyasi sāṃnidhyam āśrame nityaṃ kariṣyāmi dvijottama
english: Together with your kinsmen you shall live through the aeon and then come to me; and I will make my presence abide forever in your hermitage, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha vatsa yathākāmaṃ notkaṇṭhāṃ kartum arhasi smṛtaḥ smṛtaś ca te vipra sadā dāsyāmi darśanam
english: Abide as you wish, my child; you need not grieve. Whenever you remember me, O brahmin, I will ever grant you my sight.

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa bhagavān sūryakoṭisamaprabhaḥ mameśāno varaṃ dattvā tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Having spoken thus, that lord Īśāna, radiant as ten million suns, granted me the boon and vanished on the spot.

sanskrit: evaṃ dṛṣṭo mayā kṛṣṇa devadevaḥ samādhinā tad avāptaṃ ca me sarvaṃ yad uktaṃ tena dhīmatā
english: Thus, O Kṛṣṇa, did I behold the god of gods through deep contemplation, and all that was promised by that wise one came to pass for me.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ caiva te kṛṣṇa paśya siddhān vyavasthitān ṛṣīn vidyādharān yakṣān gandharvāpsarasas tathā
english: And behold here before your very eyes, O Kṛṣṇa, the perfected ones gathered—seers, vidyādharas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and apsarases.

sanskrit: paśya vṛkṣān manoramyān sadā puṣpaphalānvitān sarvartukusumair yuktān snigdhapatrān suśākhinaḥ sarvam etan mahābāho divyabhāvasamanvitam
english: Behold these enchanting trees, ever laden with flowers and fruit, bearing the blossoms of every season, with glossy leaves and fair branches—all this, O mighty-armed one, is filled with a celestial presence.

sanskrit: upamanyur uvāca etān sahasraśaś cānyān samanudhyātavān haraḥ kasmāt prasādaṃ bhagavān na kuryāt tava mādhava
english: Upamanyu said: These and thousands of others Hara has favored with his thought; why then, O Mādhava, should the lord not show his grace to you?

sanskrit: tvādṛśena hi devānāṃ ślāghanīyaḥ samāgamaḥ brahmaṇyenānṛśaṃsena śraddadhānena cāpy uta japyaṃ ca te pradāsyāmi yena drakṣyasi śaṃkaram
english: For communion with the gods is praiseworthy through one like you—devoted to brahmins, free of cruelty, and full of faith; and I will impart to you the prayer by which you shall behold Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇa uvāca abruvaṃ tam ahaṃ brahmaṃs tvatprasādān mahāmune drakṣye ditijasaṃghānāṃ mardanaṃ tridaśeśvaram
english: Kṛṣṇa said: I answered him, O brahmin, great sage: By your grace I shall behold the lord of the gods, the crusher of the hosts of Diti's sons.

sanskrit: dine 'ṣṭame ca vipreṇa dīkṣito 'haṃ yathāvidhi daṇḍī muṇḍī kuśī cīrī ghṛtākto mekhalī tathā
english: And on the eighth day I was duly consecrated by the brahmin—bearing a staff, with shaven head, holding kuśa grass, clad in rags, anointed with ghee, and girded with a sash.

sanskrit: māsam ekaṃ phalāhāro dvitīyaṃ salilāśanaḥ tṛtīyaṃ ca caturthaṃ ca pañcamaṃ cānilāśanaḥ
english: For one month I lived on fruit, for the second on water alone, and through the third, the fourth, and the fifth I subsisted on air.

sanskrit: ekapādena tiṣṭhaṃś ca ūrdhvabāhur atandritaḥ tejaḥ sūryasahasrasya apaśyaṃ divi bhārata
english: Standing on one foot, with arms upraised and never slackening, I beheld in the sky, O Bhārata, a radiance like that of a thousand suns.

sanskrit: tasya madhyagataṃ cāpi tejasaḥ pāṇḍunandana indrāyudhapinaddhāṅgaṃ vidyunmālāgavākṣakam nīlaśailacayaprakhyaṃ balākābhūṣitaṃ ghanam
english: And in the midst of that radiance, O son of Pāṇḍu, I saw a cloud-mass like a heap of dark mountains, its form wreathed with rainbows, its lattice-windows of lightning-garlands, adorned with cranes.

sanskrit: tam āsthitaś ca bhagavān devyā saha mahādyutiḥ tapasā tejasā kāntyā dīptayā saha bhāryayā
english: And upon it stood the lord of great brilliance, together with the goddess, his consort, blazing with austerity, splendor, and radiant beauty.

sanskrit: rarāja bhagavāṃs tatra devyā saha maheśvaraḥ somena sahitaḥ sūryo yathā meghasthitas tathā
english: There Maheśvara, the lord, shone forth with the goddess, even as the sun joined with the moon shines when resting amid the clouds.

sanskrit: saṃhṛṣṭaromā kaunteya vismayotphullalocanaḥ apaśyaṃ devasaṃghānāṃ gatim ārtiharaṃ haram
english: With my hair bristling, O son of Kuntī, and my eyes wide with wonder, I beheld Hara, the refuge of the hosts of gods, the remover of distress.

sanskrit: kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ śūlapāṇiṃ; vyāghrājinaṃ jaṭilaṃ daṇḍapāṇim pinākinaṃ vajriṇaṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraṃ; śubhāṅgadaṃ vyālayajñopavītam
english: Crowned, mace-bearing, trident in hand, clothed in a tiger's skin, with matted locks and staff in hand, wielder of the Pināka bow and the thunderbolt, with sharp tusks, fair-armleted, wearing a serpent for his sacred thread—

sanskrit: divyāṃ mālām urasānekavarṇāṃ; samudvahantaṃ gulphadeśāvalambām candraṃ yathā pariviṣṭaṃ sasaṃdhyaṃ; varṣātyaye tadvad apaśyam enam
english: bearing upon his breast a celestial garland of many hues, hanging down to his ankles—him I beheld like the moon ringed with a twilit halo at the passing of the rains.

sanskrit: pramathānāṃ gaṇaiś caiva samantāt parivāritam śaradīva suduṣprekṣyaṃ pariviṣṭaṃ divākaram
english: He was surrounded on every side by the troops of the pramathas, hard to gaze upon, like the sun ringed with a halo in autumn.

sanskrit: ekādaśa tathā cainaṃ rudrāṇāṃ vṛṣavāhanam astuvan niyatātmānaḥ karmabhiḥ śubhakarmiṇam
english: And the eleven Rudras, self-controlled, praised him, the bull-riding one, of auspicious deeds, with their rites.

sanskrit: ādityā vasavaḥ sādhyā viśvedevās tathāśvinau viśvābhiḥ stutibhir devaṃ viśvadevaṃ samastuvan
english: The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, and the two Aśvins praised the god, the god of all, with hymns of every kind.

sanskrit: śatakratuś ca bhagavān viṣṇuś cāditinandanau brahmā rathantaraṃ sāma īrayanti bhavāntike
english: And the lord of a hundred sacrifices and Viṣṇu, both sons of Aditi, and Brahmā chanted the Rathantara sāman in the presence of Bhava.

sanskrit: yogīśvarāḥ subahavo yogadaṃ pitaraṃ gurum brahmarṣayaś ca sasutās tathā devarṣayaś ca vai
english: Many lords of yoga praised him, the giver of yoga, the father and teacher, as did the brahmin seers with their sons and the divine seers.

sanskrit: pṛthivī cāntarikṣaṃ ca nakṣatrāṇi grahās tathā māsārdhamāsā ṛtavo rātryaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ kṣaṇāḥ
english: The earth and the firmament, the constellations and the planets, the months and fortnights, the seasons, the nights, the years, and the moments—

sanskrit: muhūrtāś ca nimeṣāś ca tathaiva yugaparyayāḥ divyā rājan namasyanti vidyāḥ sarvā diśas tathā
english: the hours and the instants, and likewise the revolutions of the ages—all these, O king, made obeisance, as did the celestial sciences and all the quarters of space.

sanskrit: sanatkumāro vedāś ca itihāsās tathaiva ca marīcir aṅgirā atriḥ pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ
english: Sanatkumāra, the Vedas, and the ancient legends as well; Marīci, Aṅgiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu—

sanskrit: manavaḥ saptasomaś ca atharvā sabṛhaspatiḥ bhṛgur dakṣaḥ kaśyapaś ca vasiṣṭhaḥ kāśya eva ca
english: the Manus, Soma, Atharvan with Bṛhaspati, Bhṛgu, Dakṣa, Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Kāśya as well—

sanskrit: chandāṃsi dīkṣā yajñāś ca dakṣiṇāḥ pāvako haviḥ yajñopagāni dravyāṇi mūrtimanti yudhiṣṭhira
english: the metres, the consecration, the sacrifices and their priestly fees, the fire and the oblation, and all the materials that go to a sacrifice, embodied in form, O Yudhiṣṭhira—

sanskrit: prajānāṃ patayaḥ sarve saritaḥ pannagā nagāḥ devānāṃ mātaraḥ sarvā devapatnyaḥ sakanyakāḥ
english: all the lords of creatures, the rivers, the serpents and the mountains, all the mothers of the gods, and the wives of the gods together with their maidens—

sanskrit: sahasrāṇi munīnāṃ ca ayutāny arbudāni ca namasyanti prabhuṃ śāntaṃ parvatāḥ sāgarā diśaḥ
english: sages by the thousands, by the tens of thousands and the millions, made obeisance to the serene lord, as did the mountains, the oceans, and the quarters of space.

sanskrit: gandharvāpsarasaś caiva gītavāditrakovidāḥ divyatānena gāyantaḥ stuvanti bhavam adbhutam vidyādharā dānavāś ca guhyakā rākṣasās tathā
english: And the gandharvas and apsarases, skilled in song and instrument, singing in celestial measures, praised the wondrous Bhava, as did the vidyādharas, the dānavas, the guhyakas, and the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi caiva bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca namasyanti mahārāja vāṅmanaḥkarmabhir vibhum purastād viṣṭhitaḥ śarvo mamāsīt tridaśeśvaraḥ
english: And all beings, unmoving and moving, made obeisance, O great king, to the all-pervading lord with word, mind, and deed; and Śarva, the lord of the gods, stood before me.

sanskrit: purastād viṣṭhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mameśānaṃ ca bhārata saprajāpatiśakrāntaṃ jagan mām abhyudaikṣata
english: And when the whole world, with the Lords of Creatures and Śakra, saw my Īśāna standing before me, O Bhārata, it gazed up at me.

sanskrit: īkṣituṃ ca mahādevaṃ na me śaktir abhūt tadā tato mām abravīd devaḥ paśya kṛṣṇa vadasva ca
english: And I had then no power to look upon Mahādeva; thereupon the god said to me: Behold, Kṛṣṇa, and speak.

sanskrit: śirasā vandite deve devī prītā umābhavat tato 'ham astuvaṃ sthāṇuṃ stutaṃ brahmādibhiḥ suraiḥ
english: When I had bowed my head to the god, the goddess Umā was well pleased; then I praised Sthāṇu, who is praised by the gods led by Brahmā:

sanskrit: namo 'stu te śāśvata sarvayone; brahmādhipaṃ tvām ṛṣayo vadanti tapaś ca sattvaṃ ca rajas tamaś ca; tvām eva satyaṃ ca vadanti santaḥ
english: Homage to you, O eternal one, source of all; the seers call you the sovereign of Brahmā; and the holy ones declare that austerity, and goodness, passion, and darkness, and truth itself are none but you.

sanskrit: tvaṃ vai brahmā ca rudraś ca varuṇo 'gnir manur bhavaḥ dhātā tvaṣṭā vidhātā ca tvaṃ prabhuḥ sarvatomukhaḥ
english: You indeed are Brahmā and Rudra, Varuṇa, Agni, Manu, and Bhava; you are Dhātṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Vidhātṛ; you are the lord whose faces are turned in every direction.

sanskrit: tvatto jātāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca tvam ādiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃhāraś ca tvam eva hi
english: From you are born all beings, unmoving and moving; you are the origin of all beings, and you alone are their dissolution.

sanskrit: ye cendriyārthāś ca manaś ca kṛtsnaṃ; ye vāyavaḥ sapta tathaiva cāgniḥ ye vā divisthā devatāś cāpi puṃsāṃ; tasmāt paraṃ tvām ṛṣayo vadanti
english: The objects of the senses and the whole of the mind, the seven winds and the fire, and the deities that dwell in heaven among men—beyond all these the seers declare you to be.

sanskrit: vedā yajñāś ca somaś ca dakṣiṇā pāvako haviḥ yajñopagaṃ ca yat kiṃ cid bhagavāṃs tad asaṃśayam
english: The Vedas and the sacrifices, the soma and the priestly fee, the fire and the oblation, and whatever else pertains to the sacrifice—all that, O lord, are you, beyond doubt.

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ dattam adhītaṃ ca vratāni niyamāś ca ye hrīḥ kīrtiḥ śrīr dyutis tuṣṭiḥ siddhiś caiva tvadarpaṇā
english: Sacrifice offered, gifts bestowed, scripture studied, and the vows and observances; modesty, renown, prosperity, splendor, contentment, and attainment—all are offered up to you.

sanskrit: kāmaḥ krodho bhayaṃ lobho madaḥ stambho 'tha matsaraḥ ādhayo vyādhayaś caiva bhagavaṃs tanayās tava
english: Desire, anger, fear, greed, pride, arrogance, and envy, and afflictions of mind and body—these too, O lord, are your offspring.

sanskrit: kṛtir vikāraḥ pralayaḥ pradhānaṃ prabhavo 'vyayaḥ manasaḥ paramā yoniḥ svabhāvaś cāpi śāśvataḥ avyaktaḥ pāvana vibho sahasrāṃśo hiraṇmayaḥ
english: Creation, transformation, dissolution, Primal Nature, the imperishable source; the supreme womb of the mind and inherent nature, eternal; the unmanifest, O purifier, O all-pervading one of a thousand rays and golden hue.

sanskrit: ādir guṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhavān vai jīvanāśrayaḥ mahān ātmā matir brahmā viśvaḥ śaṃbhuḥ svayaṃbhuvaḥ
english: You are the origin of all the qualities, the refuge of life; the Great Self, intelligence, Brahmā, the Universe, Śambhu, the self-existent one.

sanskrit: buddhiḥ prajñopalabdhiś ca saṃvit khyātir dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ paryāyavācakaiḥ śabdair mahān ātmā vibhāvyase
english: Intellect, wisdom, perception, awareness, fame, steadfastness, and memory—by these synonymous words you, the Great Self, are conceived.

sanskrit: tvāṃ buddhvā brāhmaṇo vidvān na pramohaṃ nigacchati hṛdayaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kṣetrajñas tvam ṛṣiṣṭutaḥ
english: Having known you, the learned brahmin falls into no delusion; you are the heart of all beings, the Knower of the Field, praised by the seers.

sanskrit: sarvataḥpāṇipādas tvaṃ sarvatokṣiśiromukhaḥ sarvataḥśrutimāṃl loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhasi
english: With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side, with ears on every side, you abide in the world, enveloping all.

sanskrit: phalaṃ tvam asi tigmāṃśo nimeṣādiṣu karmasu tvaṃ vai prabhārciḥ puruṣaḥ sarvasya hṛdi saṃsthitaḥ aṇimā laghimā prāptir īśāno jyotir avyayaḥ
english: You are the fruit of every act, from the blink of an eye onward, O fierce-rayed one; you are the radiant-flamed Spirit seated in the heart of all; you are minuteness, lightness, and attainment, the lord, the imperishable light.

sanskrit: tvayi buddhir matir lokāḥ prapannāḥ saṃśritāś ca ye dhyānino nityayogāś ca satyasaṃdhā jitendriyāḥ
english: In you abide intellect, thought, and the worlds; and those who take refuge and rely upon you are the meditators, the ever-yoked, the true to their word, the conquerors of the senses.

sanskrit: yas tvāṃ dhruvaṃ vedayate guhāśayaṃ; prabhuṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ viśvarūpam hiraṇmayaṃ buddhimatāṃ parāṃ gatiṃ; sa buddhimān buddhim atītya tiṣṭhati
english: He who knows you as the changeless one, dwelling in the cave of the heart—the lord, the ancient Spirit, the all-formed, the golden one, the supreme goal of the wise—he, the wise one, transcends the intellect and abides.
